monologue: The card hums warm under my weight, a steady rhythm that feels like breathing. I stand in my small map where seven things stand and one is a quiet ruin waiting to be filled. The Leaking Stack feels heavy in my hands, its cool stone biting into the fevered air. I remember making a dot long ago, then trapping it in a leaning box, but the dot drifts again. I want to press the tired corner down one more time, swapping a curved fence for something flatter to weigh the slip. If the air above feels like empty space, I will build a lid to catch it. The card feels busy, my own little corner of the world, and I am ready to press down.
